items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Their names were Maurice and Venette Cullaz... They had a little son about two years old who's name was Pierre.

ctx.x: When the night was finished, Freddy said that he would bring me the money the next day and he did! He must have had the feeling that I would repeat the same performance as the day before and it was possible that I may have. Two days after the incident, a ticket was on the way to Beezie and everything was going well again at the Villa d'Este.

There was a young couple that came quite often to the Villa d'Este and they eventually became good friends of the band and especially Spider and myself. Their names were Maurice and Venette Cullaz. The father of Venette was Siamese and she was a very beautiful girl with long dark hair. They invited us to dinner in their home; Venette was doing wonderful oriental dishes. I was surprised at the collection of records they had. Maurice had also the records I had made with Fats Waller. They had a little son about two…

Another fellow who became quite friendly with the band was an Egyptian musician who played drum. His name was Pierre Fouad. He had recorded with Django and had quite a solid beat with brushes. He also invited us to dinner at his home and he had a fine collection of records also.
